candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care, printed p.7 / PDF p.11; Appendix A printed p.20 / PDF p.24, Assignment, Delegation and Supervision; Establishing Priorities printed p.21 / PDF p.25
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — assignment based on acuity, client needs, and staff competency
candidate.educational_objective: Base nursing assignments on client acuity and care needs while matching required tasks to personnel who are competent to perform them.

options.A: Client acuity and needs together with each staff member's competency to perform the required care
options.B: Room location alone so assignments are geographically convenient
options.C: Client insurance status rather than clinical care needs
options.D: Staff seniority alone without considering client needs or competency

candidate.rationale: The 2026 NCSBN Test Plan directs nurses to prioritize care based on client acuity and, under Assignment, Delegation and Supervision, to assign tasks based on client needs to personnel with competency to perform them. Therefore A contains the clinically relevant assignment factors. B and C use nonclinical factors, and D ignores both client needs and staff competency.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Client acuity and needs, together with staff competency for required tasks, are relevant factors for prioritizing and assigning nursing care.
candidate.source_locator: Management of Care, printed p.7 / PDF p.11: 'Prioritize the delivery of client care based on acuity'; Appendix A, printed p.20 / PDF p.24, Assignment, Delegation and Supervision: identify tasks based on client needs and assign appropriate tasks to personnel with competency to perform tasks
candidate.source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
candidate.stem: A charge nurse is making client assignments for the oncoming shift. Which information should guide the assignments?
